PullRequest.Title: ci: reuse the runner's Node.js for server tests and retry stalled downloads
PullRequest.Body:

Stops the Browser and Remote PR jobs from downloading Node.js from nodejs.org, and makes `fetchUrl` retry a stalled download after 30 seconds instead of 5 minutes.

## Why

Since 04:22 UTC on Oct 28, 12 macOS PR jobs have timed out: 8 `macOS / Browser` and 4 `macOS / Remote`. Both start the server out of sources, and `npm run gulp node` downloads the server's Node.js from nodejs.org. nodejs.org returns the headers in under a second, then the body stalls. `fetchUrl` only gives up after its 5-minute timeout, so three or four stalls use up the 20-minute step:

```
10:46:30 Start fetching https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/node-v24.22.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz (1 retry)
10:46:30 Fetch completed: Status 200. Took 567 ms
10:51:31 Fetching https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.1/node-v24.22.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz failed: AbortError: This operation was aborted
...
11:01:35 ##[error]The action '🧪 Run integration tests (Remote)' has timed out after 20 minutes.
```

The WebKit job shows only `Storing log files into '…/server'` and then the timeout, because the integration harness hides the server's output. 8 of the 12 runs passed on rerun.

#344728 and #344714 handle the same nodejs.org stalls in Azure Pipelines. They don't touch the GitHub Actions PR workflows or `.build/node`.

## Change

- **Reuse the runner's Node.js.** New `build/azure-pipelines/common/useRunnerNodeForServer.ts`:
  - `.nvmrc` and `remote/.npmrc` both pin 24.22.1, and `actions/setup-node` already installs that version on every runner.
  - When the runner's Node.js is the version that `remote/.npmrc` pins, the script copies it to the path that `build/lib/node.ts` prints.
  - `npm run gulp node` and `scripts/code-server.*` then skip the download.
  - On a version mismatch, for example mid-upgrade, it does nothing and the download happens as before.
  - If the copy fails, it removes the platform folder again. Any failure only logs a `::warning::`, so the step never fails and the tests still run and download Node.js.
- **Workflow step.** `pr-darwin-test.yml`, `pr-linux-test.yml` and `pr-win32-test.yml` run the script before the integration tests. It only runs in the jobs that start the server: macOS and Linux `Browser` and `Remote`, and Windows `Browser`, `Remote (integration)` and `Remote (smoke)`.
- **Stalled downloads.** `fetchUrl` reads the body as a stream. When no data arrives for 30 seconds, it aborts with `No data received for 30000 ms` and retries. The 30-second header timeout and the 5-minute timeout for the whole download are unchanged. This applies to every build download that uses `fetchUrl`, not just Node.js.

## Notes for reviewers

- The copied binary comes from the runner's tool cache, which `actions/setup-node` fills with repackaged official builds. It isn't verified against `build/checksums/nodejs.txt`. That's fine for tests out of sources; product builds still download and verify.
- On Linux x64, the download path patches the ELF load alignment so the binary runs under WSL1. The runner's copy skips that patch, which doesn't matter because the Linux PR jobs don't run under WSL1.
- No new cache entry and no change to `pr-node-modules.yml` or the missing-cache detection.

## Validation

- `cd build && node --test lib/test/fetch.test.ts lib/test/useRunnerNodeForServer.test.ts`: **passed** (2 tests). One test covers a body that stalls (aborted after the idle timeout) and one that arrives slowly but steadily (completes). The other covers copy, already present, version mismatch, and a failed copy.
- Forced failure (a file where the `v24.22.1` folder goes): the script printed ``::warning::Cannot use the runner's Node.js for the server, so `npm run gulp node` downloads it: ENOTDIR …`` and **exited 0**.
- `cd build && node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`, which parse these workflows: **passed** (25 tests).
- `cd build && npm run typecheck`: **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- build/lib/fetch.ts build/lib/test/fetch.test.ts build/azure-pipelines/common/useRunnerNodeForServer.ts build/lib/test/useRunnerNodeForServer.test.ts`: **passed**.
- Pre-commit hygiene: **passed**.
- Manual run on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1:
  - `node build/azure-pipelines/common/useRunnerNodeForServer.ts` copied Node.js to `.build/node/v24.22.1/darwin-arm64/node`, which prints `v24.22.1`.
  - A second run reported it as already present.
  - `npm run gulp node` then finished in 3 ms without downloading.
- Parsing the three workflows with js-yaml: every job gets the step through the shared `steps` anchor. Only the Browser and Remote jobs listed above satisfy its condition.
- **Not yet run:** the GitHub Actions jobs themselves. This PR changes workflow and `.ts` files, so change detection runs every core test job. The Browser and Remote logs should show `Copied the runner's Node.js v24.22.1 …` and no nodejs.org fetch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browser and Remote PR jobs prepare the server runtime before integration or smoke tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added workflow step must finish before the test command. It synchronously resolves the expected server Node path and, on a cold matching-version job, copies the runner binary; this replaces the later server-start path's Node.js download and extraction. On version mismatch or helper failure, the later download remains on the test-start critical path as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the current Node executable once to evaluate `build/lib/node.ts` and print the expected server Node path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one short subprocess per selected Browser/Remote CI job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No preparatory subprocess ran; the server startup later resolved/downloaded Node through the gulp task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess is newly on the pre-test critical path but performs only local module startup and one small file read; it is fixed-cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read `remote/.npmrc`, test the destination, create its directory, and copy the runner's Node executable when versions match.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One metadata/read sequence per selected job and at most one binary copy on a cold matching-version job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A cold `.build/node` path remained absent until the server-start gulp task downloaded and wrote/extracted Node.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous copy delays the test command by local copy time, but substitutes for a larger network download plus archive extraction or binary write on the same scenario.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the pinned Node runtime from nodejs.org through `fetchUrls` when `.build/node` is absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one logical download per cold job, with sequential retries on failure. After the diff it is zero when setup-node has the pinned version, and unchanged on version mismatch or helper failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every cold Browser/Remote job reached this network download when starting the server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This boundary blocks server startup. The diff removes it from the common matching-version path rather than introducing or moving it earlier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One server Node runtime per selected CI job. The three shared workflow step lists select a fixed set of Browser/Remote jobs; there is no per-test or per-file multiplication within a job.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within each job, path resolution, filesystem checks, and copying are synchronous and serial. Jobs run independently according to GitHub Actions scheduling; the change adds no in-job burst or shared unbounded concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: If the exact `.build/node/v<version>/<platform>-<arch>/node[.exe]` path already exists, the helper performs no copy and the later gulp node task also skips download. On the normal clean-job miss with a matching setup-node version, one local copy populates that path. Version mismatch and copy failure deliberately leave a miss, so the unchanged later download occurs; there is no negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow conditions, setup-node placement, helper synchronization, and gulp's directory-existence gate directly establish the before/after path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact local binary-copy duration and runner cache warmth vary by platform, but the fixed one-copy cost is clearly bounded and replaces a network download/extraction on the common cold path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fixed local preparation work removes a slower and failure-prone network boundary for matching versions, while warm and mismatch paths remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build tooling downloads Node runtimes, marketplace extensions, and GitHub release assets through `fetchUrl`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each caller awaits the complete response buffer before checksum verification and downstream extraction/processing, so network body progress and full-body buffering remain on build or dependency-setup critical paths. The new idle timer is also on that path only as a cancellation guard.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one HTTP response and retry it after errors or body inactivity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a successful logical download; up to 11 sequential requests under the pre-existing retry limit. The diff changes the inactivity detection point from the five-minute whole-download limit to 30 seconds without data, not successful-request cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same HTTP request and retry path existed, but a response that returned headers and then stopped sending bytes occupied the critical path until the five-minute whole-download timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete body is required before checksum and downstream processing. On a stalled body, the change shortens the time before retry; on a progressing body, the idle timer refreshes and does not add another boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Accumulate response bytes into memory, concatenate them into a Buffer, and optionally hash the complete Buffer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful asset; retained bytes are O(asset size), followed by one checksum pass when configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Native `response.arrayBuffer()` materialized the full body and `Buffer.from` wrapped it before the same optional checksum and downstream processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Full buffering and checksum remain prerequisites for returning the Vinyl file. The explicit chunk reader enables idle detection; the prior `response.arrayBuffer()` also required a complete in-memory body, so the diff does not establish a new asymptotic buffering cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales linearly with downloaded bytes and with the number of caller-requested assets. Each logical asset uses one request when successful; an idle/erroring asset can make up to 11 attempts through the existing sequential retry recursion.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single `fetchUrl` reads one response at a time and retries serially after a one-second delay. `fetchUrls` may map caller-provided URL arrays, but reviewed production calls here pass one URL per logical asset; no new aggregate concurrency or fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `fetchUrl` has no internal cache. Node's `.build/node` directory and workflow caches can avoid calls before reaching it; extension/build callers control their own cache or invocation. Successful and failed fetches are not memoized or coalesced by this change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the network critical path, retry limit, serial scheduling, and linear full-body buffering; insufficient evidence that explicit chunk accumulation materially regresses memory versus the prior native full-body conversion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Asset sizes and network stall prevalence vary, and repository evidence does not establish a materially higher peak allocation than native `arrayBuffer()` for normal downloads. The stalled-read latency mechanism itself is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced performance issue. Progressing downloads retain the prior one-request, O(bytes) behavior, while stalled bodies release the network critical path earlier. This also constitutes a concrete performance fix, though the internal regression-fix recorder rejected both submission attempts.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all seven changed files and complete diff pages. Traced the CI runtime-reuse path and every production `fetchUrl` caller, including subprocess, filesystem, network, buffering, retry, cache, and concurrency behavior. No actionable performance regression was introduced; the PR removes a cold-job Node download and adds progress-sensitive cancellation for stalled bodies. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
